Fixes: c2594d804d5c ("macb: Common code to enable ptp support for MACB/GEM")

diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/cadence/macb_ptp.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/cadence/macb_ptp.c
index c9e77819196e..d91f7b1aa39c 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/cadence/macb_ptp.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/cadence/macb_ptp.c
@@ -357,8 +357,10 @@ void gem_ptp_remove(struct net_device *ndev)
 {
 	struct macb *bp = netdev_priv(ndev);
 
-	if (bp->ptp_clock)
+	if (bp->ptp_clock) {
 		ptp_clock_unregister(bp->ptp_clock);
+		bp->ptp_clock = NULL;
+	}
 
 	gem_ptp_clear_timer(bp);
 
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

### Files Modified

**`drivers/net/ethernet/cadence/macb_ptp.c`**
- In function `gem_ptp_remove()`, after calling `ptp_clock_unregister(bp->ptp_clock)`, a new line is added to set `bp->ptp_clock = NULL`.

### Relationship Between Changes

The single change addresses a use-after-free vulnerability. The PTP clock pointer (`bp->ptp_clock`) was previously left pointing to freed memory after the clock was unregistered (during interface close). Since `gem_get_ts_info()` (and other functions) checks `bp->ptp_clock` for non-NULL before accessing it, a concurrent `ethtool` call could still dereference the stale pointer after the clock was destroyed. By setting the pointer to `NULL` immediately after unregistration, any later access sees the pointer as invalid and skips the use of the freed clock, preventing the use-after-free.

Set the PTP clock pointer to NULL after unregistering.

Fixes: c2594d804d5c ("macb: Common code to enable ptp support for MACB/GEM")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Fedor Pchelkin <pchelkin@ispras.ru>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260316103826.74506-1-pchelkin@ispras.ru
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

Here is the root cause:
The PTP clock pointer (bp->ptp_clock) is not set to NULL after being unregistered in gem_ptp_remove(). When the interface is closed, the clock structure is freed, but the dangling pointer remains, allowing a subsequent ethtool get_ts_info call to dereference it and cause a use-after-free.

Here is the patch:
 
 void gem_ptp_remove(struct net_device *ndev)
 {
 	struct macb *bp = netdev_priv(ndev);
 
-	if (bp->ptp_clock)
+	if (bp->ptp_clock) {
 		ptp_clock_unregister(bp->ptp_clock);
+		bp->ptp_clock = NULL;
+	}
 
 	gem_ptp_clear_timer(bp);
 
 	dev_info(&bp->pdev->dev, "%s ptp clock unregistered.\n",
 		 GEM_PTP_TIMER_NAME);
 }
